items.bold: TRUMP ARRIVED IN BEIJING. TRUMP-XI SUMMIT LIVE TODAY. Iran dominates agenda. Tim Cook, Elon Musk in CEO delegation.
items.text: CNN (4 hours ago) confirmed: US President Donald Trump arrived in China's capital and was welcomed with a ceremony replete with pomp and pageantry for the start of a high-stakes visit carrying global consequences. Trump will meet with Chinese leader Xi Jinping today to discuss trade, tech, Taiwan, and Iran. CNN: "Iran's shadow: The US-Israeli war with Iran, and ensuing global energy crisis, looms over the trip. Trump is expected to encourage Xi to push China-ally Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and agree to a peace deal." Travelling with Trump: top officials and more than a dozen business leaders including Tim Cook (Apple) and Elon Musk. Trump told reporters Tuesday before departing: "We're going to have a long talk about it." Also said: "I don't think we need any help with Iran" — downplaying dependency while acknowledging the conversation.

items.bold: ARAGHCHI VISITED BEIJING BEFORE TRUMP — Iran lobbied Xi directly. Now at BRICS Delhi for Jaishankar bilateral.
items.text: CNN (4 hours ago) confirmed: Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi traveled to Beijing BEFORE Trump's arrival, "underscoring close ties between the two countries." Iran's ambassador to China told state media: "China can be an important force for reducing tensions between Tehran and Washington." Added that Beijing was "not merely an economic partner" but part of Iran's "political balancing" against external threats. This confirms what the tracker predicted: Iran was actively lobbying Beijing not to concede to US pressure on Hormuz before Trump arrived. Araghchi is now in Delhi for the BRICS Foreign Ministers meeting — giving EAM Jaishankar the bilateral the tracker has flagged as India's most important diplomatic opportunity of the war. The Araghchi-Jaishankar bilateral in Delhi while Trump meets Xi in Beijing is the defining simultaneous diplomatic moment of Day 76.

items.bold: US OFFICIALS WORRIED: Xi "holds the cards." China ordered companies NOT TO COMPLY with Iran sanctions. Beijing in stronger position.
items.text: CNN (4 hours ago) and CNBC confirmed: some US officials have expressed concern that Trump is "walking into a meeting where Xi holds the cards — and that the Chinese leader may use that leverage to get what he wants on an issue important to Beijing: Taiwan." CNBC confirmed: China ordered companies not to comply with US sanctions on Iranian oil. China also hosted Iran's FM before Trump arrived — a clear signal of where Beijing's loyalties sit. CNBC analysis: "China has — so far — been less visible" in the war's economic impact. China gains a positional advantage the longer the war drags on. Beijing residents CNN spoke to voiced "little appetite for China becoming more involved to end the Iran war" — reflecting the broader Chinese instinct for neutrality. If Xi extracts Taiwan concessions from Trump in exchange for Iran pressure: complex geopolitical trade-off with long-term consequences far beyond Hormuz.

items.bold: TRUMP NET APPROVAL LOWEST OF HIS TWO TERMS. S&P +7.3% since war — stock market paradox. Real economy pain growing.
items.text: CNBC (13 hours ago) confirmed: Trump's net approval rating has fallen to the lowest of his two terms, according to CNBC's All-America Economic Survey. Gas at $4.50. Diesel up 61%. And yet: the S&P 500 has risen 7.3% since February 27, just before the US and Israel attacked Iran. CNBC: "Trump is banking little political goodwill from the stock market that keeps grinding to records." The paradox — stock market up, approval rating down — reflects that Main Street (gas prices, real economy) and Wall Street (large-cap earnings, defence stocks) are experiencing the war differently. For Trump's political calculus heading into Beijing: the approval rating decline is the dominant signal. A deal that lowers gas prices is worth more to Trump politically than any trade deal Xi can offer. Trump's political survival argument for a Beijing Hormuz breakthrough is maximum.

items.bold: CHATHAM HOUSE: War "handed China advantages it could not have dreamed of." India driven toward Beijing by Trump tariffs.
items.text: Chatham House (2 days ago) confirmed: "For Beijing, President Donald Trump is the gift that keeps on giving. His decisions have handed China's leadership advantages of which it cannot have dreamed before he arrived in the Oval Office for the second time." Specifically: Trump cancelled clean technology subsidies (allowing China to extend its lead), slapped tariffs on allies including Vietnam and India (driving them towards Beijing), called NATO into question, sided with Russia on Ukraine, and "now he has tied up the US military and his own attention in a war with Iran which he cannot easily end." The Iran war = Chinese strategic gain. India being driven toward Beijing by Trump's India tariffs is particularly significant — India is simultaneously a BRICS host (China-led multilateral) and a QUAD member (US-aligned) in the same week. India must carefully navigate this diplomatic moment.

military.t: US OFFICIALS WORRIED: Xi "Holds the Cards" — May Extract Taiwan Concessions. China Ordered Iran Sanctions Non-Compliance.
military.d: CNN (4 hours ago) confirmed: some US officials have expressed concern that Trump is "walking into a meeting where Xi holds the cards — and that the Chinese leader may use that leverage to get what he wants on an issue important to Beijing: Taiwan." China is Iran's largest oil buyer and largest trade partner. The longer the war continues, the more valuable China's Iran leverage becomes — Beijing can extract concessions from Washington in exchange for applying pressure on Tehran. CNBC: China ordered companies not to comply with US sanctions on Iranian oil — a direct counter to Trump's sanctions campaign. Beijing residents voiced "little appetite for China becoming more involved" in the war. Chatham House: "China has some leverage with Iran but will want something from the US in return." The Taiwan-for-Iran-pressure trade is the core geopolitical risk of the Beijing summit.

military.t: TRUMP NET APPROVAL Lowest of Two Terms. Gas $4.50. S&P +7.3% Since War. Main Street vs Wall Street Paradox.

For Trump's Beijing calculation: the approval rating decline (driven by gas prices and real economy pain) is more politically urgent than any trade deal Xi can offer. A Hormuz deal that lowers gas prices is the single highest-value political outcome Trump can achieve in Beijing. This gives Trump maximum incentive to get a result — but Xi knows this, giving Beijing more leverage.

military.t: CHATHAM HOUSE: War "Handed China Advantages It Could Not Have Dreamed Of." India Driven Toward Beijing by Trump Tariffs.

CNBC analysis: Trump's "tendency to improvisation and desire for wins injects extra uncertainty" into the Beijing meeting. Trump's allies fear he will make "long-term strategic concessions for a handful of soybean, sorghum and Boeing jet sales." India being driven toward Beijing by Trump tariffs is particularly significant for India's diplomatic positioning this week — India is simultaneously QUAD-aligned (US) and BRICS host (China-led) — hosting Araghchi at BRICS while the US tries to use China to pressure Iran. India must navigate both tracks carefully.

assessment.body:
Thursday 6:45 AM IST. Day 76. The day the war's trajectory will be determined.

TRUMP IN BEIJING — THE SUMMIT IS LIVE
Trump arrived Wednesday night, welcomed with pomp and pageantry.
Meeting with Xi Jinping today.
Iran dominates the agenda alongside trade, Taiwan, tech, AI.
CEO delegation: Tim Cook (Apple), Elon Musk, 12+ business leaders.
Trump publicly: "I don't think we need any help with Iran."
Trump privately: "We're going to have a long talk about it."

ARAGHCHI PRE-POSITIONED IN BEIJING
Iran's FM visited Beijing BEFORE Trump arrived — lobbied Xi directly.
Iran ambassador to China: relationship "too strong for US to overcome."
China ordered companies not to comply with US Iran sanctions.
Beijing residents: "little appetite for China becoming more involved."
After Beijing: Araghchi flew to Delhi for BRICS Foreign Ministers.
Jaishankar-Araghchi bilateral: underway or imminent today.

XI HOLDS THE CARDS
Some US officials worried — Xi may extract Taiwan concessions for Iran pressure.
China is Iran's largest oil buyer AND largest trade partner.
The longer the war continues: the more valuable China's leverage becomes.
Trump's approval at lowest of two terms — politically desperate for gas price relief.
Xi knows this. Beijing knows this. The negotiating asymmetry is real.

WHAT INDIA HAS TODAY
Araghchi at BRICS Delhi: direct diplomatic access to Iranian FM.
Trump-Xi Beijing: outcome determines Brent direction.
India is the only country simultaneously engaging BOTH sides of this negotiation today.
Jaishankar must raise: Indian tanker coordination, fertiliser corridor, 280 seafarers, OMC crude.
This is India's most diplomatically significant day since February 28.

THREE SUMMIT SCENARIOS FOR INDIA
SCENARIO A — Xi agrees to pressure Iran on nuclear:
Brent falls $10-15 immediately. Nifty +500-1,000 pts (23,900-24,400). Rupee strengthens.
SCENARIO B — Inconclusive:
Brent holds $104-107. Nifty flat to -200. Stalemate continues.
SCENARIO C — Xi extracts Taiwan concessions:
Geopolitically complex. Brent may fall (Iran signal) but strategic uncertainty spikes.
India must decide how to respond to a US-China deal that trades Taiwan for Hormuz.

VERDICT: Day 76 is the day. Every thread of the 76-day war converges today in two rooms — the Great Hall of the People in Beijing and the BRICS Foreign Ministers table in Delhi. In Beijing: Trump asks Xi to help end the war that is killing Trump's approval ratings and costing American consumers $4.50/gallon. In Delhi: Jaishankar sits across from Araghchi — the Iranian FM who visited Beijing before Trump arrived to make sure Xi didn't cave. India is at the centre of both conversations simultaneously. Whatever happens today will determine India's energy, economic, and diplomatic trajectory for the rest of 2026.

featured.desc: Chokepoint control is no longer binary (open/closed) but a layered spatial contest spanning seabed topology, island sovereignty, electronic warfare, and visibility asymmetry. The cartography of maritime control in the 2026 crisis.

featured.title: Geopolitics of LPG Supply in India
featured.desc: How India's LPG import dependency on the Gulf creates acute vulnerability during the West Asia War. Explores Hormuz exposure, alternative supply routes, and policy imperatives for energy security in a blockade scenario.

featured.title: Geopolitics of Fertiliser Supply in India
featured.desc: India imports 30%+ of its fertilisers via the Strait of Hormuz. This paper maps the supply chain risks to kharif and rabi crops, the strategic case for diversification, and what a prolonged blockade means for food security.
